Jasmine — high level: feasible, but we need to choose between two approaches. I sketched scenarios in the attached CSO sheet. TL;DR:

Scenario A — Single invoice, itemized credits by region (preferred for buyer UX)
  - Invoice = consolidated USD invoice to CloudSync (CloudSync PO).
  - Offer PDF = shows credits applied per-region (US West / EU Central) as separate line items.
  - Reseller margin = explicit line item showing 12% channel fee; Redwood books full revenue, we note reseller pass-through in invoice notes.
  - Pros: clean for CloudSync accounting; Procurement happy.
  - Cons: might require manual ops step to ensure EU tax stamping/region-specific VAT handling on attached reconciliation (we can add a note).

Scenario B — Two billing instances, single PO mapping (engineering heavy)
  - We create two billing buckets per region, credits applied locally, and a consolidated invoice generated by ops glue.
  - Pros: cleaner tax compliance per region.
  - Cons: more engineering + slow for first-time setups; likely a one-off implementation fee.

Notes: Reseller margin as visible line item is OK. We should confirm reseller tax id and whether they want net remittance vs. vendor-managed pass-through. If partner wants direct invoicing from Redwood to reseller (versus pass-through), that's a different legal/finance flow.

I've attached CSO-partner-margin-sheet.xlsx with recommended language for the offer PDF and a sample breakdown; see tab "CloudSync-proposal".

-ben

Proposal (recommended - low ops lift): Scenario A (single invoice, itemized credits by region)
  - Redwood will issue a consolidated USD invoice to CloudSync (single PO reference DW-4821-AZ).
  - The Private Offer PDF and attached reconciliation will include per-region credit lines: "US West - usage credit: $X", "EU Central - usage credit: $Y".
  - Reseller/partner margin: Redwood will show a separate line item: "Stratus Partners channel fee (12%)" with the numeric amount. Redwood will retain contract/revenue, and the invoice will include "Partner payout instructions" as a note.
  - Tax handling: since invoice is consolidated, Redwood will include a region breakdown and a supplemental reconciliation file (CSV) so CloudSync can allocate costs. If EU VAT is required, we will append tax annotations; however, if CloudSync prefers the EU-region invoice with local tax stamping, we recommend Scenario B (two billing instances).

Next steps if this works for you:
  1) Confirm Stratus Partners' tax ID and whether Redwood should remit partner payouts or CloudSync will handle pass-through.
  2) Sign the attached PrivateOffer_CloudSync_v1.docx (I will send a DocuSign link once you confirm).
  3) If approved, I will loop finance to create the consolidated invoice template and the per-region reconciliation CSV.

Attachments: PrivateOffer_CloudSync_v1.docx (draft offer), CSO-partner-margin-sheet.xlsx (breakdown)
